name: Core AI (LLM runtime, Core ML successor)
baseline: Core ML LLM conversions on the Neural Engine (CoreML-LLM), and MLX Swift as the fastest third-party alternative
verdict_reason: Core AI's GPU engine decoded several times faster than the Core ML Neural Engine conversion on iPhone 17 Pro. Its headline 2.47x lead over MLX holds only for a 0.6B model built with one export toolchain. After re-export it is 1.1x, at 8B it is a near tie, and MLX wins the MoE model by 28%.
tier_reason: Third-party harness with public code, raw logs and environment pins; Core AI cells use Apple's own llm-benchmark release build.
claimed_speedup: iPhone 17 Pro, Qwen3-0.6B: 193.3 tok/s cold vs 37.7 for Core ML (different sessions); M4 Max vs MLX: 1,121 vs 455 tok/s (2.47×) with the macOS-26 export, ~500 vs 455 (1.1×) after re-export, Qwen3-8B 94 vs 90 (1.05×), gpt-oss-20b MoE 78.1 vs 100.2 (MLX +28%); same recipe gives a 2.2× slower artifact after the macOS 27 beta upgrade
workload: Batch-1 greedy decoding of 4-bit Qwen3 0.6B to 8B, Gemma and Mistral models: 128-token short-chat on iPhone, 512-token prompt and 1024 generated tokens on Mac.
hardware: iPhone 17 Pro (A19 Pro); Mac Studio (M4 Max)
os: iOS 27 beta; macOS 26 and macOS 27 beta
toolchain: coreai.llm.export and coreai-build from Apple's coreai-torch; mlx-lm 0.31.3 for the MLX column
one_liner: Apple's Core ML successor in iOS 27/macOS 27; decodes LLMs several times faster than Core ML conversions and ties MLX on dense models.
how_it_is_fast: PyTorch models are exported with coreai-torch into .aimodel bundles. A dynamic-shape export runs on a pipelined GPU engine that overlaps dispatch with compute, which matters most for small models. A static-shape export targets the Neural Engine. On iOS the bundle is compiled ahead of time for the specific GPU architecture.
use_it_when: New apps targeting iOS 27 / macOS 27 that would otherwise ship a Core ML LLM conversion
Small dense models where dispatch overhead dominates and the pipelined GPU engine has its largest lead
You want Apple's first-party runtime without bundling MLX
skip_it_when: Apps that must run on iOS 26 or earlier
Mixture-of-experts models, where MLX was 28% faster
Long contexts on iPhone: the harness hit an iOS KV cap of 1,024 and jetsams under its deep protocol
caveats: All measurements on beta OS releases from June to September 2026
Results depend on the export environment: the same recipe produced a 2.2x slower artifact after a macOS 27 beta upgrade
The iPhone Core AI vs Core ML cells come from sessions a day apart, which the README says should not be turned into ratios
Warm re-capture of the 0.6B iPhone bundles was blocked by a coreai-build regression in July
Single third-party harness; no Apple-published performance numbers were checked
tradeoffs: The compute unit is fixed by the export shape, not chosen at runtime
iOS bundles must be compiled ahead of time per GPU architecture
The Neural Engine path used about 1.2 GB on iPhone, several times the Core ML conversion's footprint

evidence.quote: recipe produces a 2.2× slower artifact after the macOS 27 beta upgrade
Core AI jetsams under the standard deep protocol
